subject: MAP + Eval plan: unit economics, prefetch/caching & batching assumptions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: Kim Patel <kim.patel@pulseguide.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + Eval plan: unit economics, prefetch/caching & batching assumptions

Hi Darcy / Kim —

Thanks for the sync today — attaching an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a simple unit-economics workbook so we can validate numbers against your traffic profile. High level asks here so the MAP has clear acceptance criteria for the evaluation phase: 

- Evaluation window: 2 weeks of production-like traffic (we recommend a 10k daily active conversion sample).
- Tokens / $: baseline estimate in the workbook uses 0.8 tokens per user-turn (NLP prompt + completion average) and a model cost of $0.0009/token for the chosen q4-8 quantized variant — please review and flag if your prompts are longer.
- Prefetch / caching: we propose prefix caching for repeated context (TTL = 5m default), with conservative cache-hit modeled at 18% for the first pass. That reduces average tokens/generated by ~12% in our sim.
- Batching assumptions: 20–60ms batching window targeting 8–16 requests/batch for typical burst profiles; we included sensitivity rows in the workbook.
- Acceptance KPIs for close: tokens/$ within 15% of model, tail latency P95 < 450ms, correctness pass-rate on your eval set > 92%.

Next steps: please confirm (A) that the sample traffic is feasible, (B) whether caching of identifiers is allowed under your data policy (we note PHI constraint in red in the MAP), and (C) a target kickoff date for the eval.

Attachments: PulseGuide_MAP_v1.0.pdf, unit_econ_model_pulseguide.xlsx

Thanks — I left the MAP purposely light so we can iterate quickly.

Best,

- On caching: we cannot cache PHI or direct identifiers. We can cache de-identified prefixes or non-PHI context. Does your proposed prefix cache allow a de-identification step?
- Latency: we need to ensure P95 under 400ms if possible — how aggressive is the batching to hit your unit-econ?

Can you loop in an infra/SE contact who can explain the caching policy in a bit more detail? Also copy of the MAP would be helpful with the redline track.

Hi Darcy — looping in a few technical clarifications.

On Mon, Jul 28, 2025 at 11:03 AM Darcy Liu <darcy@pulseguide.com> wrote:
> Thanks Camila — quick responses inline.

Short answers first: the $0.0009/token is our hosted API estimate for the quantized model class after typical committed-capacity discounts (not including marketplace surcharge). The workbook models both hosted and dedicated numbers; see the "pricing_scenarios" tab.

Caching and PHI: the prefix cache is configurable to only cache de-identified context. Recommended pattern: run a lightweight de-id filter client-side (we include a simple regex-based step in the MAP), then cache the sanitized prefix. That keeps PHI off the cache and satisfies typical compliance requirements. We'll include an explicit cache-allowed/forbidden column in the next MAP revision.

Batching vs latency tradeoff: the 20–60ms batching window yields good token efficiency at typical QPS. In our internal tests:
- 20ms window -> avg batch size 6 -> token cost ~ baseline*0.94, P95 ~ 380–420ms depending on model length
- 60ms window -> avg batch size 14 -> token cost ~ baseline*0.81, P95 ~ 480–520ms

If you need P95 < 400ms consistently, we recommend a hybrid policy: keep the primary route at 20–25ms batching with aggressive prefix caching and an "economy" fallback that bursts batching during non-critical flows. That hits your latency target while preserving most econ gains.

Attached: quick excerpt from our bench runs and a pointer to the unit_econ_model_pulseguide.xlsx. I'll update the MAP to surface the PHI-safe cache flow and the two-tier batching policy.

Cheers,
